summary: Reconciles eight validated stage-1 proposals in the vehicle_physics scope into one conservative engine map. The dominant decision is a single per-vehicle object family (F1CVehicle) that consolidates the six independently proposed views of the same 0x48C0 vehicle-slot object: VehiclePhysicsBody (vehicle_physics_01:2), Vehicle (vehicle_physics_02a:0), VehiclePhysicsBody (wave_001_vehicle_physics_01:0), F1CVehicle (wave_001_vehicle_physics_02:10), VehiclePhysicsObject (wave_001_vehicle_physics_03:0) and Vehicle (wave_001_vehicle_physics_04:0). That merge is justified by interlocking call relationships (0x004E4570->0x004E4790, 0x004E4790->0x0043E230, 0x004C73F0->0x004E24A0, 0x004E45B0->0x004E5F60, 0x004F0430->0x004C73F0), the shared physics-mode gate field this+0x32BC, the shared orientation/world block 0x34B0..0x34DC, and overlapping time/state fields 0x48B4/0x48B8 - but common ownership is a reconciliation decision, not packet-proven, and is recorded as a conflict. VehiclePhysicsNode merges the suspension-strut solver chain (vehicle_physics_01:0) with WheelSurfaceResolver (wave_001_vehicle_physics_01:1) on the shared +0x130/+0x134 316-byte-stride strut array plus shared callees 0x004FAF60/0x004FB260. TireModelData merges the 0x004F34E0 constructor (vehicle_physics_02a:1) with its sub-helpers 0x004F2B50/0x004F31F0 (wave_001_vehicle_physics_04:8); VehicleTireModel (0x0043C250) is kept separate because no call or field evidence ties it to 0x004F34E0. PhysicsSolverState merges 0x00579CCF (zero-init) with 0x00578F76 (row-identity init) because both operate on the same global 0x008D2120..0x008D3978 double-precision dynamics-matrix region. VehicleControlState (fields up to +0x5F68) is kept separate from F1CVehicle because +0x5F68 exceeds the 0x48C0 vehicle-slot stride and it holds a physicsBodyPtr at +0x15F0. All owners are DERIVED/GUESS worker proposals; no trust is promoted; the packet's own contradictions (mass vs anti-roll use of +0x3510/+0x3514, tracked-point vs wing-flag role of +0xCC8/+0xD0C, the 0x32BC vs 0x32C8 mode-dispatch discrepancy, the shared 0x94..0xA0 band on Vehicle vs TireModel, and the 0x130/0x134 array appearing on both the vehicle and the strut-node object) are preserved in conflicts rather than erased.

engine_subsystems.name: VehiclePhysicsCore
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle physics simulation and control: the per-vehicle object carrying the mode-gated timestep, wheel/suspension/tire force solving, wheel-space transform chain, setup-vector propagation, reset/cleanup and collision damage feedback; the suspension strut array solver chain (contact solving, swept detection, distance-falloff force propagation, wheel-surface resolution); the per-wheel spring/damper force kernel; and the control/steering state object (input mapping, steering geometry, torque/brake distribution, pit-limiter and lap transitions).

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleConfigurationAndTireSetup
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Vehicle and tire configuration loading: the .SVM/.HDV line parser and its section readers (damage, engine, engine-map fields, per-wheel brake/suspension, damping-direction validation), the config validator, the suspension setup section reader, the tire-model constructor and the per-session tire-model initializer, plus the suspension-physics snapshot copier.

engine_subsystems.name: CollisionAndVehicleLifecycle
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Collision handling and per-vehicle/session lifecycle support: collision-feature normal resolution, broadphase AABB list building, collision object-list sorting/filtering/draining against the global free pool, the generic list and node record layouts, the track-environment physics parameter profiles, the per-car physics state constructor, the qualifying tire-usage event encoder, the vehicle-list/name-list containers rebuilt from the global vehicle array, and the AI-side relative-speed and gear-shift helpers.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleInputAndMathSolverState
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Input smoothing/gear selection, velocity/angular-velocity integration, coordinate-frame math, and solver/state lifecycle: the vehicle input controller and integrator, matrix/vector transform helpers, the inverse-3x3 coordinate-transform workspace, the global double-precision physics dynamics-matrix region (row-identity and zero-init), the per-frame physics state buffer clearer, the per-frame wheel parameter evaluator, and the suspension-array motion/proximity helpers.

canonical_type_families.name: F1CVehicle
canonical_type_families.responsibility: The per-vehicle object (0x48C0 vehicle-slot stride at global 0x5EC6D8). Carries the physics-mode selector at +0x32BC, the slot-live/mode dword at +0x32C8, the wheel-space orientation matrix +0x34B0..+0x34D0 and world position +0x34D4..+0x34DC, per-wheel dynamics records at +0x35A0 (62-dword stride), climb/vibration fields +0x3994..+0x39C4, integration fields +0x3498..+0x34AC, the driver-info region +0x4620..+0x48BC, and the last-setup/last-frame time fields +0x48B4/+0x48B8. Methods cover per-frame init/timestep/integration (0x00439210, 0x0043E230, 0x00441450, 0x00441650, 0x004C73F0, 0x004E45B0, 0x004F0430), wheel/suspension/tire force solving (0x004E5470, 0x004E5F60, 0x004E8010 via wrapper 0x004E4910), wheel-space transforms (0x004E23D0, 0x004EF6C0, 0x004EFB20, 0x004F1650, 0x004E9BD0), reset/cleanup/audio (0x004E0800, 0x004E09E0, 0x004E4570, 0x004E4790, 0x004E3360, 0x004C6E80, 0x004C79E0, 0x004C7BF0), camera/setup snapshot (0x004E49B0), yaw recovery (0x004F1FE0, 0x004F2320), climb adjust (0x004EFA40), motion/proximity propagation (0x004FB260, 0x004FB2E0) and collision feedback (0x004EC1A0). Merge of six proposals (see conflict entries).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: The union of six proposals touches overlapping bands of one large per-vehicle struct: mode/slot dwords +0x32BC/+0x32C8, orientation/world +0x34B0..+0x34DC, wheel record arrays +0x35A0/+0x35B0 (62-dword stride) and per-wheel force fields +0x3664/+0x375C/+0x3854/+0x394C (248-byte stride, wheel-block base +0x35AC), per-frame integration +0x3498..+0x34AC, climb/vibration +0x3994..+0x39C4, driver-info +0x4620..+0x48BC. Field samples are boundary clues, not a complete layout; many per-wheel, camera-snapshot (+0x3510..+0x39F0) and collision-zone (+0x3D48..+0x3EB8) fields are left unnamed. The 0x94..0xA0 motion band also appears on TireModel (see conflict); no cross-family field identity is assumed. The packet assigns the same offsets conflicting roles across proposals (0x32BC vs 0x32C8 mode, 0x35A0 vs 0x35B0 wheel base) - a layout engineer must resolve these before building; the 0x48AC property slot is recalculated every frame elsewhere so external pokes to it do not persist.

canonical_type_families.name: VehiclePhysicsNode
canonical_type_families.responsibility: The suspension strut array object: owns the strut array (base this+0x134, count this+0x130, 316-byte stride) and runs the per-strut contact solver (0x00401340), the swept-strut contact solver (0x00401910), the per-frame force-propagation chain with grip-multiplier and per-strut finalization (0x00401C90), and the per-wheel surface-resolution query pass against the spatial structure dword_5EA2C0 (0x00404250). Merge of VehiclePhysicsNode (vehicle_physics_01:0) and WheelSurfaceResolver (wave_001_vehicle_physics_01:1): both operate on the same +0x130/+0x134 316-byte-stride array and both call the same 0x004FAF60/0x004FB260 helpers. The maximum-propagated-force output is at +0x148; grip scale at +0x170 and phase flag at +0x174.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: The strut-array header (+0x130 count, +0x134 base, stride 316) is the only container identity evidence; element-relative offsets (strut +24 travel scale, +112/+116 penetration, +120..+128 gravity-compensated force, +136/+140 propagation results, +144 candidate force, +148..+156 wheel position, +268 linked-node, +272 contact-feature pointers) come from source:raw prose and are NOT emitted as field entries - treat as boundary clues and verify against the .c before building. Grip-scale formula 1.0 - (flt_8AFEE8 + flt_8AFEEC)*0.5 stored at +0x170 and phase-flag reset +0x174 = -1 on exit are DERIVED from 0x00404250.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleControlState
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Vehicle control and steering state object: maps raw controller input into steering/throttle/brake commands, applies steering damping and per-wheel steering geometry, runs collision/obstacle avoidance, lap/position transitions and pit-limiter state, and distributes torque/brake to the wheels (0x004441F0); per-wheel steering geometry update with trig-table noise and secondary-state steering flag (0x00442060). Kept separate from F1CVehicle: it holds a physicsBodyPtr at +0x15F0 and a field at +0x5F68 that exceeds the 0x48C0 vehicle-slot stride.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Control outputs (steering +0x0, throttle +0x8, brake +0x10, offset +0x20), raw input bytes (+0x68/+0x70), collision probe pointers (+0xB4/+0x11C), physics body pointer (+0x15F0), pit-limiter (+0x1D30) and lap (+0x1EF0) state, brake/torque scales (+0x1554/+0x155C/+0x1564), wheel contact array (+0x15BC/+0x15C0) and secondary state flags (+0x5F68). The packet's field evidence is spread across two functions; the +0x1F00 dereferenced chain (tire block at *(*(this+0x1F00)+0x32E0)+0x78/+0x7C/+0x84) is a separate sub-object layout and is carried in unresolved_evidence_refs, not modeled here. The shared +0x1F00 offset range overlaps F1CVehicle members in the packet; identity is unproven and the overlap is recorded in conflicts.

canonical_type_families.name: WheelSpringDamperState
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-wheel spring/damper force computation (0x004E3D00): builds an orthonormal frame from the suspension axis (near-vertical fast path and 2D fallback), computes contact-frame forces, updates spring stiffness and force magnitude, tracks contact-patch displacement, clamps forces to the friction/grip circle and writes the force components back along the wheel local axes. Consumed by the per-frame vehicle force pass (0x004E5470) and the tire-brush model service.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Fifteen per-wheel field samples: suspension-axis (+0x38/+0x3C/+0x40), wheel velocity (+0x18/+0x1C/+0x20), spring stiffness +0x48, force magnitude +0x4C, force-active flag +0x50, simplified-rotation flag +0xBC, contact position (+0xC4/+0xC8) and force outputs (+0xD8/+0xDC/+0xE0). These are boundary clues on the per-wheel spring/damper state struct; the second parameter a2 (contact-patch frame, 9 floats) layout is inferred from usage and not described by the packet.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleBodyObject
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Object reached by dereferencing this[0] of the yaw-recovery/audio paths (packet 'obj' base): carries the post-process input state dword (obj+0x4064), an off-track distance (obj+0x4170, FLT_MAX sentinel), a mode/lap-line field (obj+0x3450) and the instance id (obj+0x4894) used to gate the vehicle sound trigger. Data-layout family with no methods; identity with F1CVehicle is not established.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Four obj-relative fields are sampled (+0x3450 lap-line index, +0x4064 post-process input state, +0x4170 off-track distance, +0x4894 instance id). The packet keeps the obj base distinct from the this base of F1CVehicle; the two are not merged.

canonical_type_families.name: MotionLineEntity
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Position+direction line object consumed by the proximity computation (0x004FB2E0): the own data block at *(this+0x10C) and target1 at *(this+0x110) expose position at +0x94/+0x9C, direction at +0xA4/+0xAC, and target1 carries an internal self pointer at +0x110. Data-layout family with no methods.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Nine field samples across the two bases: *(this+0x10C) position/direction (+0x94/+0x9C/+0xA4/+0xAC) and *(this+0x110) position/direction (+0x94/+0x9C/+0xA4/+0xAC) plus the self pointer (+0x110). Names (Position/Direction) are GUESS; the layout is evidenced only by these dereferences.

canonical_type_families.name: ProximityTargetEntity
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Second proximity target object (packet base *(this+0x114)): a different layout from the motion-line objects, exposing position at +0x0/+0x8 only. Used by VehicleProximity's target2 projection (0x004FB2E0). Data-layout family with no methods.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Two field samples (+0x0/+0x8) named PositionX/PositionY as GUESS. The layout difference from MotionLineEntity is preserved (distinct base, distinct offsets).

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleTireModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-session tire-model initialization object: builds per-wheel compliance matrices and stiffness/damper/thermal state, applies tire brand and compound, computes front/rear suspension compliance and attach-point geometry, allocates the interpolated tire-curve table, seeds wear/thermal session tables and ends by setting init markers this+0x30=-2, this+0x34=3 (0x0043C250). Kept separate from TireModelData: 0x0043C250 is a runtime session initializer with no call or field connection to the 0x004F34E0 constructor; both are invoked from 0x0043E050 but that alone does not prove the same object.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Init markers +0x30/+0x34 (write), HUD disable flag +0x70 (write), tire brand +0x1458 and compound +0x145C ids (write), curve-table buffer +0x1CFC (write) with entry count +0x1D08 (read), wear seed +0x1DB4 (read/write). Field samples are boundary clues; the per-wheel compliance matrix and thermal-state layout behind the tire block is documented in proposal prose only and is not field-evidenced. The tire-wear-mode switch (dword_7CEA5C 0=disable, 1..3=scale) is a separate state machine on this object.

canonical_type_families.name: TireModelData
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-vehicle tire model configuration data constructed once (ABI lead Tire_Model_Data_Init, LEGACY): handle sentinels (primary 0, others -1), compound count 15, friction/camber/slip coefficient seeding, zero-init sub-structures, four 66-dword physics-default sub-structs and a config-path string copy through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc from global 0x005EA438. Methods: bulk constructor 0x004F34E0, physics-defaults initializer 0x004F2B50 and zero-init helper 0x004F31F0 (both called by 0x004F34E0). Merge of TireModelData (vehicle_physics_02a:1) with the TireModel helpers (wave_001_vehicle_physics_04:8) on the direct caller/callee relationship.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Header handles +0x0..+0x3C (sentinels/compound count) and zero-init region +0x90..+0xA4 are field-evidenced; the coefficient pairs (+0x13A8..+0x13CC) and the physics-default block (DWORD indices 18..65) are sample clues only. The offset space (0x0..+0x13CC) numerically overlaps the F1CVehicle offset space; the packet keeps the bases separate (evidence) but embedding the tire model data within a larger vehicle allocation is possible and unproven - see conflict. Owners of 0x004F2B50/0x004F31F0 are 'TireModel' in wave_001_vehicle_physics_04, grouped here on the caller relationship to 0x004F34E0.

canonical_type_families.name: TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Line-by-line .SVM/.HDV vehicle configuration parser (ABI lead The_svm_hdv_Vehicle_File_Parser, LEGACY): opens the file in binary-read mode, validates the format on a first pass, dispatches named sections (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, per-wheel corners, Basic) to section readers, resolves secondary files, and normalizes range/setting pairs into the output vehicle-state struct. Invoked by the config validator and by per-vehicle setup paths.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Parser 'this' fields (tire_compound_rpm_multiplier +0x8, rules_setting +0x34, garage_display_flags +0x38, loaded-flag bytes +0x1EC/+0x2F8/+0x4D4, engine-map scale doubles +0x674/+0x67C, wheel_drive_classification +0x13C0, forward_gear_count +0x13C4) are the internal setup struct, sampled as boundary clues. The output vehicle-state struct (a3) layout is only partially mapped (byte flags +6540/+6544/+6556/+6565/+6536/+6537/+6564, engine-scale doubles +6548/+6552); names and sizes inferred from usage. The config-token string globals (0x005D4E90..0x005D572C) and the Wheel%d/Part%d key templates are referenced by address only.

canonical_type_families.name: EngineSectionParser
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Parses the [ENGINE] section of the vehicle engine configuration: fuel/inertia, idle/launch/rev-limit (RPM to rad/s), the RPM-torque curve, lifetime and thermal parameters, with idle/launch/curve ordering and point-count validation logged in non-server sessions. Calls the engine-map field-definition registration (0x004F3C10) and is called by TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser. Owner is the packet's named 'EngineSectionParser' (no class proposal ref); the family is a reconciliation container for a required function.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Engine field samples (+0x68C idle min, +0x694 idle max, +0x6A0 idle clamp, +0x6AC/+0x6B4 launch, +0x6BC rev limit, +0x6C4 point count, +0x6C8 curve base, +0x6D0/+0x6D8 torque throttle/brake, +0x12C8 optimum oil temp, +0x1310/+0x1318 lifetime RPM, +0x1320 lifetime oil temp) are boundary clues on the engine setup struct; the target pointers at +0x5488/+0x5552/+0x5616 are not field-evidenced and the layouts they index are not defined here.

canonical_type_families.name: EngineSetup
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Engine setup configuration struct whose field definitions are registered by 0x004F3C10 (rev limit, engine map, engine braking multiplier via CRTMathHelper_e1f0) during .hdv loading. The engine-field layout (+0x68C..+0x1320) is shared with EngineSectionParser; 0x004F3C10 writes into the same setup target, so the two families overlap in data. Kept separate because 0x004F3C10 and 0x004F3C80 are distinct functions with distinct roles (registration vs section parse).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: The packet proves only the linear registration structure (three range/setting pairs with RPM-scale and unit scales). Field names/offsets are GUESS boundary clues on the shared engine setup struct; the setup-target pointer is passed as an argument, not stored on a this object.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleDamageModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Flat vehicle damage configuration struct populated by ParseVehicleDamageConfig (0x004F24F0): general physics, front/rear wing, four wheels and eight detachable parts, decoded from the Physical subsection of a binary-read stream with generated Wheel%d/Part%d keys. Returns 0 on success, -1 when the stream cannot be opened. Called by TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No damage-parameter slots are field-evidenced by the packet (this+0..+132 observed in prose only); the flat struct layout is a boundary clue. Do not build on specific damage-field offsets without verifying against the .c.

canonical_type_families.name: PerWheelBrakeSuspensionDataLoader
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Parser object for per-wheel brake/suspension configuration: decodes bump/rebound travel, bump-stop, brake torque/wear/fade/thermal, pushrod values and the Celsius-to-Kelvin brake optimum (+0xB8) from the shared token stream, then normalizes 11 range/setting pairs into the corner block (704-byte stride by wheel index) with a deg-to-rad camber multiplier. Called by TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Only +0xB8 (brake optimum temperature, Kelvin) is field-evidenced; the remaining double-array element mapping is derived from token names and the 704-byte corner-block stride/offsets 176..816 are observed from the body but not field-evidenced - boundary clues only.

canonical_type_families.name: HdvFileParser
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Vehicle .hdv loading helper: validates damping-direction signs per axis (0x004F3240) by parsing three damping doubles into a 24-byte triple selected by direction index (0-5) and logging per-axis warnings when the sign opposes expected motion, suppressed in session type 5. Class identity is GUESS; no field layout is evidenced.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No this-field layout is evidenced; the function parses into argument buffers. The six force-apply log strings are referenced by address only; their text content is not recovered.

canonical_type_families.name: WheelParameterEvaluator
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame wheel parameter evaluator (0x004F69E0): computes linear combinations of three scalar inputs against coefficient/bias doubles (this+0x3F4..+0x530) producing two force magnitudes (fabs of +0x444/+0x47C) and a combined output. Called from the per-frame physics path (0x004E5F60), suspension setup (0x004390A0) and 0x00430600.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: The nine double samples (+0x3F4, +0x3FC, +0x444, +0x47C, +0x4AC, +0x518, +0x520, +0x528, +0x530) are boundary clues; the packet proves only the linear structure, not the physical meaning. The a6 output is written but never read inside the function; its downstream consumer is outside the packet.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleConfigValidator
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Validates a vehicle configuration by parsing the default and override SVM/HDV files into byte_7C56C0 (0x00433ED0); returns 0 only when both parses succeed and commits the override path into this+0/this+8 string slots when the commit flag is set. Called from 0x004336F0 and 0x0046E5C0.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Two string-slot fields at +0x0 (read) and +0x8 (write) are evidenced; the parse buffer byte_7C56C0 is a global, not a this field. Cost-display backup dword_7C56C4 = dword_7D0450 is taken before parsing.

canonical_type_families.name: SuspensionSetup
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Parsed suspension setup configuration: setup index, body anchor/rotation reference, min/max position and orientation (deg-to-rad), and a growing spring array (capacity +0x94, count +0x98, pointer +0x9C) of 100-byte classified spring entries (sliding/normal/free-damping = 0/1/2). Populated by 0x00435410; also calls the physics state-buffer clearer 0x004358F0.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Setup fields +0x0..+0x8C (anchor, min/max orientation) and spring-array header +0x94/+0x98/+0x9C are sampled; the spring element layout (head mass double at obj+0xAC, reciprocal at obj+0xB4) is a boundary clue on the target struct. Growth rule is +3 slots of 100 bytes via the allocation wrapper.

canonical_type_families.name: VehicleListContainer
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Holds two linked lists rebuilt from the global vehicle array (dword_8AC390 count, dword_8AC394 base, stride 1060): the vehicle list (this+0x0..0xC, 12-byte nodes wrapping 176-byte entries, 0x00415780) and the deduplicated commentary name list (this+0x10..0x1C, 0x004159B0).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Ten list-header fields (+0x0..+0x1C) and two node fields (obj+0x0 data, obj+0x8 flag) are sampled. Entry data (176-byte vehicle entries, 172-byte name entries) is boundary clue only; the caller 0x00415090 is outside the packet and the commentary-list bookkeeping role is inferred.

canonical_type_families.name: RelativeSpeedCalculator
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Computes signed longitudinal (dot product) or lateral (2D cross product) relative speed against a target vehicle for AI steering; stores magnitudes in this+0x24 and a normalized relative speed in this+0x30 (0x00423B10). Called from AI steering (0x004270A0).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Target pointer at +0x0; target object fields obj+0x34E0/+0x34E8 (position) and obj+0x34F8/+0x3500 (velocity) are read on the target object, not this. The target object type is not named.

canonical_type_families.name: GearShiftController
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame AI gear-shift control (0x00426330): blocks shifts while the shift timer is positive, forces reverse in driverStatus==6 and neutral in carConditions==2 pit mode, and upshifts on RPM threshold with a 0.8 traction guard, capped at max gear.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Nine vehicle-state fields are sampled (+0x37CC/+0x38C4 traction, +0x39A0 rpm, +0x39FC gear, +0x3A04 max gear, +0x3A10 shift timer, +0x3A18 threshold, +0x3D6C car conditions, +0x4510 driver status). The literal gear requests (-1 reverse / 0 neutral) and the JUMPOUT(0x4F62E6) downshift tail outside the packet are inferred from surrounding guards.

canonical_type_families.name: Matrix3x3
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Row-major 3x3 double matrix used as a linear-algebra transform; 0x004361D0 multiplies a difference vector (a3 - a2) by the matrix this[0..8] and writes the result into a4, returning a4. Pure function with no callees. Used by the per-frame physics initializer (0x00439210), the integration driver (0x00441650) and the velocity/angular-velocity integrator (0x00459AE0).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Nine double elements +0x0..+0x40 are GUESS-named m00..m22; the layout is the only field evidence and the matrix is read-only. This is a stateless math helper; grouping into a 'class' is by shape only.

canonical_type_families.name: SuspensionPhysicsSnapshot
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame snapshot of suspension physics state (0x0043BC20): copies two collision-geometry blocks from a3, evaluates quadratic-spring/force/torque terms from the descriptor a2, then copies force/torque parameters, wheel/damper blocks and quad/spring-damper results into the snapshot struct. Called by the tire-model initializer 0x0043C250.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Sampled fields include state flag +0x1900, force params +0x1910/+0x1914, torque params +0x1938..+0x1944, force-rate block +0x17A8..+0x17C4, and mirror spring/quad doubles +0x1C24..+0x1C4C. The destination copy regions (this+6200/+6300, six 24-byte loop copies and their tails) have no packet field entries; internal layout is inferred from copy sizes only. The duplicate re-copies (source lines 74-93) are treated as redundant double-writes with unknown semantic significance.

canonical_type_families.name: PhysicsStateBuffer
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Small physics state buffer object cleared per-frame (0x004358F0): zeroes dwords 0..38 of the 40-dword buffer, frees the heap pointer at +0x9C through the free wrapper (0x00587BCF) and nulls it, returning the previous pointer. Called from the suspension setup reader (0x00435410), the wheel-dynamics init (0x0043E230) and a constructor stub (0x004353F0).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Single field +0x9C (heap buffer pointer, read/write) is evidenced; the 40-dword buffer content is unspecified. The free-wrapper identity (0x00587BCF) is confirmed by callee evidence.

canonical_type_families.name: CollisionFeatureSolver
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Resolves the oriented collision normal for a query position from the spatial-grid collision feature's plane coefficients (0x0044C550): derives { -(v8*v6), v8, -(v8*v7) } with v8 = 1/sqrt(v7*v7 + v6*v6 + 1.0), writes it into a3 and returns the spatial-grid query result. Queries the grid via 0x0044C4C0.

canonical_type_families.responsibility: Large per-car physics state object (DWORD array up to this[998], 0x004B57F0): zeroes leading/middle arrays, sets sentinel/default blocks, forwards to sub-initializers, and configures the QPC timer block. Called from 0x004B9780.

canonical_type_families.name: QualifyingTireUsageRecorder
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Records qualifying tire-usage ring-buffer events (0x004BC060): during a qualifying session advances the ring buffer and encodes tire set in-use/discard events with a session-time payload and the tire-compound byte.

canonical_type_families.name: PhysicsSolverState

canonical_type_families.field_policy: The region is evidenced only as named globals (global:0x008D...), never as object-relative fields, so the 58 cleared locations are carried as class-level evidence references rather than modeled as fields; per-block semantics (constraint matrices, bias vectors, solver workspaces) are unestablished and common ownership is a GUESS. The selector source and call sites of 0x00578F76 are unknown (no static callers); the per-row extra element in the 0x008D3870..0x008D3978 trailing column is unresolved; whether sub_58BB10's third argument is a byte count (odd multiples of 8) or an element count is not resolvable.

state_machines.name: VehiclePhysicsMode
states: mode flag this+0x32BC == 0 -> one-time TireModelInit into dbl_7C7428 then step path (0x004E45B0)
mode flag this+0x32BC in [1,3] -> step path (HDV parse, substep clamp, force solving)
mode flag this+0x32BC == 3 -> delegate to VehiclePhysicsTimeStep (0x004C73F0) on the vehicle array slot (0x004F0430 case 3)
mode flag this+0x32BC outside [0,3] -> early return without stepping
transitions: 0x004E45B0 reads this+0x32BC: 0 selects the one-time init path; 1..3 select the step path; any other value early-returns.
0x004F0430 dispatches on the same field (cases 0-3) via jump table 0x004F0D10; case 3 delegates to 0x004C73F0 on the vehicle array at 0x5EC6D8.
VehicleClimbAdjust (0x004EFA40), VehicleDynamicsStateReset (0x004F2320) and the yaw-recovery state machine (0x004F1FE0) also branch on this+0x32BC.

state_machines.name: VehicleModeDispatch
states: mode 2 = full setup-data copy + 14 subsystem state machines
mode 3 = vibration path + 4 vibration state machines + 14 subsystem state machines
other modes = no mode-specific body; all paths converge on effect/audio flag derivation
transitions: this+0x32C8 is read each frame; values 2 and 3 dispatch distinct bodies, everything else skips the mode body (VehiclePhysicsTimeStep 0x004C73F0).
both mode bodies end in the common braking/effect/bit-flag derivation and effect-field update.

state_machines.name: GearSelection
transitions: Gear-input flag ladder at +0x1FBC..+0x20C4 selects reverse/gears 1..6 when the ladder enable byte at +0x2428 is nonzero; no flag leaves UNSELECTED (-2).
Neutral override at +0x20F0 == 0 and global byte_7D1370 == 1 force NEUTRAL (0) when the ladder is still UNSELECTED.
Gear-output slots outside the ladder (0x20F0 != 0) force the highest gear value 7.

state_machines.name: GearShiftControl
transitions: Default -> BlockedByTimer when shift_timer(this+0x3A10) > 0 (flt_59E440 zero threshold)
Default -> ReverseRequest when driverStatus(this+0x4510) == 6
Default -> PitModeNeutral when carConditions(this+0x3D6C) == 2
Default -> UpshiftReady when engine_rpm(this+0x39A0) > shift_rpm_threshold(this+0x3A18) and traction > 0.8 and current_gear(this+0x39FC) < max_gear(this+0x3A04)
Default -> DownshiftTail via JUMPOUT(0x4F62E6) when current_gear(this+0x39FC) > 1

state_machines.name: PitLimiterHudState
states: state 1 = pit limiter engaged (calls HUDElementConfig(41, 2, blend))
state 2 = pit limiter with weather-noise blend, cleared when throttle output this+0x8 < 0.8
transitions: state 0 -> 1 when pit flag dword_7CC368 set, this+0x1D34 != 0, this+0x1EF0 == 0 and vehicle state mode this+0xD0 != 2 (guard:6)
state 1 -> 2 when the pit flag clears
state 2 is cleared when throttle output drops below 0.8

state_machines.name: TireWearModeSwitch
states: wear mode 0 = wear disabled: NaN-boxed max double written to this+0x1DB8 and the four wheel wear blocks zeroed
wear modes 1..3 = wheel wear blocks scaled by flt_8ACF9C over 4 iterations
transitions: read global dword_7CEA5C: 0 selects disable, 1..3 select scaling
when session type dword_7C56A4 == 7, this+0x1DB4 is additionally divided by flt_8ACF9C

state_machines.name: SurfaceContactResolution
transitions: PrimaryQuery -> ContactAccepted when element+300 >= this+0x10 and nearest-neighbor hit (flag 1) found, storing hit pointer at element+276 and contact height at element+24
PrimaryQuery -> SecondaryPlaneTest when element+300 == 1 and element+276 still null
SecondaryPlaneTest -> ContactCleared when |signed plane distance| outside hit+0x84/+0x80 bounds (element+276 = 0, element+296 = -1)
SecondaryPlaneTest -> ContactAccepted when within bounds, copying element+296 from the hit chain

state_machines.name: VehicleYawRecovery
states: NonZero_Accumulating: state dword obj+0x4064 non-zero - accumulate frame time at this+0x4004; past 15.0 reset counters and (session 7 + audio flag) fire the audio effect
Zero_RecoveryCheck: state dword zero - off-track guard (obj+0x4170 below FLT_MAX, dword_7CE814, wheel array, +0x3994) then nearest-path and lateral-bound recovery decision
RecoveryTriggered: recovery fired - reset counters, set this+0x3D60 = 2, emit render/AI-tracking notifications in session 7
transitions: Entry -> NonZero_Accumulating when obj+0x4064 != 0 and this+0x32BC == 1 and state != 2
NonZero_Accumulating -> NonZero_Accumulating when accumulator at this+0x4004 > 15.0 (reset counters; audio effect in session 7)
Entry -> Zero_RecoveryCheck when obj+0x4064 == 0
Zero_RecoveryCheck -> RecoveryTriggered when accumulator exceeds flt_7D0A8C and off-track and lateral distance below 7.0 / bound test fails

state_machines.name: CollisionFeedbackGating
transitions: this[0] == dword_7C54E8 and gate bytes clear -> primary (player) feedback path
identity differs and restricted-mode flag != 1 -> main body runs
identity differs and race phase not in {1,3} -> main body runs
identity differs, restricted-mode flag == 1 and race phase in {1,3} -> suppressed

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionStrutArrayLayout

Per strut the solver writes contact state (penetration depths at +112/+116, gravity-compensated contact force at +120/+124/+128), force propagation results at +136/+140 and a candidate force slot at +144, reads the wheel position at +148/+152/+156 and travel scale at +24, and requires linked-node (+268) and contact-feature (+272) pointers to be non-null for contact processing. compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsStateBufferClearContract
compatibility_contracts.description: PhysicsBufferClear zeroes dwords 0..38 of the 40-dword buffer on the this object, frees the pointer stored at +0x9C through the free wrapper (0x00587BCF) and nulls it, returning the previous pointer (or 0). Callers are ConstructorStub (004353F0), SuspensionSetupSectionReader (00435410) and WheelDynamicsInit (0043E230), so the buffer is reset during vehicle/tire construction and wheel-dynamics initialization.

Auxiliary words at packet+52/+56/+59 carry flags: packet+52 bit 0x80 -> byte this+0x1069, packet+56 bits 0x8000000/0x4000000/0x2000000 -> braking byte this+0x105D and effect bytes this+0x1065/0x1067, and packet+59 bit 1 -> byte this+0x4024.

VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate reads this+0x30 for the position-change state machine, and VehiclePhysicsTimeStep branches on the vehicle mode this+0x32C8. A replacement must preserve these sentinel semantics across tire-model init, control-state updates and the physics timestep.

The wheel-force field sits at block-relative offset 0x24 (absolute 0x3664/0x375C/0x3854/0x394C): SetWheelForceParameters stores four per-wheel force parameters there, and the per-frame update initializes and reads the same block layout. A replacement must produce all 13 points and publish them to +0x1078.
